hints: Maximum velocity occurs when the rate of change of velocity (acceleration) is zero: $a = 0$.
Factor out $0.6T^{1/2}$ and solve for the non-zero root $T$.
walkthrough:
Set the acceleration to zero to find the stationary point for velocity:
$$a = 1.2T^{1/2} - 0.6T = 0$$
$$0.6T^{1/2}\left(2 - T^{1/2}\right) = 0$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the condition for maximum velocity: the derivative $\frac{dv}{dt} = a(t)$ must equal zero:
$$a(T) = 0$$
$$1.2T^{1/2} - 0.6T = 0$$

Factorize the equation:
$$0.6T^{1/2}\left(2 - T^{1/2}\right) = 0$$
Dividing by $0.6T^{1/2}$ for $T > 0$:
$$2 - T^{1/2} = 0$$
$$T^{1/2} = 2$$
Square both sides:
$$T = 2^2 = 4\text{ s}$$

hints: Find when acceleration is maximized by differentiating $a(t)$ with respect to $t$ and setting $\frac{da}{dt} = 0$.
Solve $0.6t^{-1/2} - 0.6 = 0$ to find the time $t$ of maximum acceleration.
Integrate $a(t) = 1.2t^{1/2} - 0.6t$ to find the velocity function $v(t)$, using the initial condition $v(0) = 1\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find the constant of integration.
Substitute the value of $t$ found in step 2 into your velocity function to find the velocity.
walkthrough:
Differentiate the acceleration function to locate its maximum:
$$\frac{da}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}\left(1.2t^{1/2} - 0.6t\right) = 1.2\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)t^{-1/2} - 0.6 = 0.6t^{-1/2} - 0.6$$
Set $\frac{da}{dt} = 0$:
$$0.6t^{-1/2} - 0.6 = 0 \implies t^{-1/2} = 1 \implies t = 1\text{ s}$$

Integrate acceleration to obtain the velocity function:
$$v(t) = \int \left(1.2t^{1/2} - 0.6t\right) dt = 1.2\left(\frac{t^{3/2}}{3/2}\right) - 0.6\left(\frac{t^2}{2}\right) + c$$
$$v(t) = 0.8t^{3/2} - 0.3t^2 + c$$

Apply the initial condition $v(0) = 1\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$1 = 0.8(0) - 0.3(0) + c \implies c = 1$$
$$v(t) = 0.8t^{3/2} - 0.3t^2 + 1$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Find the time of maximum acceleration by taking the derivative $\frac{da}{dt}$:
$$\frac{da}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}(1.2t^{1/2} - 0.6t)$$
Using the power rule:
$$\frac{da}{dt} = 1.2 \times \frac{1}{2}t^{-1/2} - 0.6 = 0.6t^{-1/2} - 0.6$$

Set $\frac{da}{dt} = 0$ and solve for $t$:
$$0.6t^{-1/2} = 0.6$$
Divide by $0.6$:
$$t^{-1/2} = 1$$
$$\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}} = 1 \implies \sqrt{t} = 1 \implies t = 1\text{ s}$$

Integrate acceleration to find velocity:
$$v(t) = \int a(t)\,dt = \int (1.2t^{1/2} - 0.6t)\,dt$$
$$\int 1.2t^{1/2}\,dt = 1.2 \times \frac{t^{3/2}}{3/2} = 1.2 \times \frac{2}{3}t^{3/2} = 0.8t^{3/2}$$
$$\int -0.6t\,dt = -0.6 \times \frac{t^2}{2} = -0.3t^2$$
$$v(t) = 0.8t^{3/2} - 0.3t^2 + c$$

Substitute the initial condition $v = 1$ when $t = 0$:
$$1 = 0.8(0)^{3/2} - 0.3(0)^2 + c \implies c = 1$$
So the full velocity equation is:
$$v(t) = 0.8t^{3/2} - 0.3t^2 + 1$$

Evaluate velocity at $t = 1\text{ s}$:
$$v(1) = 0.8 \times 1^{3/2} - 0.3 \times 1^2 + 1 = 0.8 - 0.3 + 1 = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
